fresh_context: Actual current sources reread, with Stage 1 and repair recheck kept separate; no writer defenses read.

headings.passage: # What the three papers establish {#ch:READING-GUIDE}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Keeps the three different contribution types as the opening question, without calling them one common experimental result.

headings.passage: ## Variable neural signals must support reliable behavior {#sec:READING-FIELD}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Variable signals and reliable behavior state the problem before defining the neuroscience field; neither phrase is dispensable to that relationship.

headings.passage: ## Persistent activity can still lose memory accuracy {#sec:READING-MEMORY}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Can still lose accuracy preserves the distinction between persistent firing and correct stored value; its modal wording avoids an all-network claim.

headings.passage: ## Eye drift points to a shared neural source {#sec:READING-EYE}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Points to and shared preserve the inference and source scope, rather than suggesting a uniquely measured integrator.

headings.passage: ## Smooth random maps explain the variety of place fields {#sec:READING-PLACE}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Smooth random maps identify the proposed account; the visible body supplies Gaussian and threshold assumptions without loading them all into an opening title.

headings.passage: ## Starting knowledge and reading paths {#sec:READING-START}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: This is a practical navigation/reference section; its topic title is sufficient to locate the required baseline and alternative paths.

headings.passage: ## How to interpret the calculations and evidence {#sec:READING-SCOPE}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Interpret calculations and evidence identifies the needed distinction between derived examples and empirical reproduction; deleting that distinction would overstate verification.

headings.passage: ## The original papers {#sec:READING-PAPERS}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: The original-paper list is a reference entry, so it needs a destination label rather than a scientific-result assertion.

headings.passage: # A thresholded Gaussian map predicts field sizes and shapes {#ch:PLACE-FIELDS}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Thresholded Gaussian map identifies the actual model family and sizes/shapes the outcomes. The opening explicitly says distributions over fields rather than next-field locations.

headings.passage: ## Thresholding a smooth Gaussian input produces place fields {#sec:PLACE-GP}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Smooth, Gaussian and thresholding are separate required model ingredients; the definition and covariance setup teach them before calculations use them.

headings.passage: ## Upcrossings count fields, with an endpoint correction {#sec:PLACE-KAC-RICE}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Upcrossings and endpoint correction identify both the counting mechanism and finite-track limit. The ensuing curve/positive-slope example teaches upcrossing.

headings.passage: ## Mean field and gap lengths separate threshold from scale {#sec:PLACE-INFERENCE}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Both field and gap means are needed to recover threshold and scale separately; removing either would hide what the inversion requires.

headings.passage: ## Why rare high fields are nearly parabolic {#sec:PLACE-RARE-PEAKS}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Needs a terminology clarification: the parabola is the input-height profile near a peak, while a field was defined as a connected region.

headings.passage: ## Geometry gives different size laws in each dimension {#sec:PLACE-SIZE-LAW}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Geometry and dimension identify the reason that one excess-height law yields different length/area/volume laws; no extra specialist label is needed.

headings.passage: ## Slices test spatial structure beyond field volume {#sec:PLACE-SLICES}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Beyond field volume states the extra evidence supplied by line/plane restrictions rather than merely listing slicing as a topic.

headings.passage: ## Why slopes at field boundaries are Rayleigh {#sec:PLACE-SLOPES}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Rayleigh is an exact distributional name here and was already supplied by the explicit earlier size law; replacing it with a vague shape word would lose the claim.

headings.passage: ## Holes distinguish maps with the same field count {#sec:PLACE-TOPOLOGY}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Holes and same field count give the reader a concrete comparison before Euler characteristic and Betti numbers are defined.

headings.passage: ## What was fitted and what was tested {#sec:PLACE-DATA}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: The question is an efficient evidence-accounting label for a heterogeneous table; its following paragraphs distinguish fitted and additionally checked summaries.

headings.passage: ## Random input weights can generate Gaussian maps {#sec:PLACE-WIRING}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Can generate preserves sufficiency without uniqueness. Gaussian is the exact statistical family; the body retains the many-input and no-dominating-input conditions.

headings.passage: # Spatial maps and memory dynamics need separate tests {#ch:SYNTHESIS}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Separate tests is the chapter conclusion, preserving map-versus-dynamics distinctions instead of promising one unified biological circuit.

headings.passage: ## The three papers constrain maps, dynamics, and movement {#sec:SYNTHESIS-QUESTIONS}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Maps, dynamics and movement are the three actual mathematical/experimental objects; constrain appropriately describes partial evidence.

headings.passage: ## How a static map can carry a moving estimate {#sec:SYNTHESIS-JOINT-CALCULATION}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Static versus moving states the relationship being demonstrated, and can preserves its status as a guide construction rather than an observed joint circuit.

headings.passage: ### Example: opposite rate changes from the same position error {#sec:SYNTHESIS-COVARIANCE-EXAMPLE}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Opposite rate changes identifies the useful sign contrast caused by one common position change; the worked numbers add more than formula substitution.

headings.passage: ## Each model needs a test matched to its claim {#sec:SYNTHESIS-EVIDENCE}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Matched to its claim distinguishes model fitting, upstream-source inference and an inequality; removing it would erase the reason the tests differ.

headings.passage: ## Related studies change assumptions and leave circuit choices open {#sec:SYNTHESIS-RELATED}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Change assumptions and leave choices open are the reason these related studies matter; specific circuit and paper names remain in their connected paragraphs.

headings.passage: ## A joint test would compare tuning maps with population fluctuations {#sec:SYNTHESIS-NEXT}
headings.deletion_and_term_judgment: Would compare marks future work and tuning/population fluctuations identify what would actually be measured, preserving the proposed-test scope.

part_title_judgments.title: Noise limits memory accuracy in continuous attractor models
part_title_judgments.evidence: Continuous attractor models gives the necessary model scope before detailed noise assumptions; the purpose explains stable-state families and surviving fluctuations.

part_title_judgments.title: Eye motion and place fields constrain different parts of a neural code
part_title_judgments.evidence: Different parts preserves the distinction between maintenance, output maps and movement evidence; the purpose explains each relationship without claiming a shared complete circuit.

fold_title_judgments.title: Derivation: normalization and higher size moments
fold_title_judgments.judgment: Retain: normalization and moments are exact probability terms, and the displayed integral defines the intended moments. The visible mean/inverse-scale equations let readers skip the check.

fold_title_judgments.title: Source check: three printed steps in the supplement
fold_title_judgments.judgment: Retain: identifies an optional source check rather than a required new result. The paragraph states apparent errors carefully and does not claim author confirmation or matching simulation mistakes.

fold_title_judgments.title: Independent check: recover field width from its boundary slope
fold_title_judgments.judgment: Retain: tells which previously derived quantity is checked by the slope route. The term independent refers to the second derivation, not statistically independent slopes.

fold_title_judgments.title: Derivation: the Gaussian determinant average and its integrals
fold_title_judgments.judgment: Retain: determinant has already been linked to local spatial/gradient volume conversion. Gaussian and determinant are needed exact terms for this calculation; replacing them would conceal the operation.

term_order_judgments: Gaussian process and joint-Gaussian covariance meanings precede derivative independence in the crossing calculation.
q, sigma and gain a are given before rate, size and cutoff conversions.
Gamma is defined before the moved generalized mean; U and beta are introduced before the folded moment substitution.
Hessian is defined before determinant averages, and Euler characteristic and Betti counts before signed densities.
Rayleigh has the explicit earlier size-density form before its boundary-slope use.
Expected-rate functions and common displacement are introduced before the synthesis covariance.
Continuous attractor in the Part title is a preview; the Part purpose explains its stable-state family, and Chapter 1 teaches it before reasoning depends on the term.

findings.passage: Why rare high fields are nearly parabolic
findings.failed_check: A title uses field for a different object from the definition the chapter relies on.
findings.deletion_test: The parabolic local approximation is needed for the width law, so deleting this point would remove the reason the next equations follow. Keep the contribution and name the profile it describes.
evidence: sec:PLACE-GP defines each connected piece of A_q as a model place field.
sec:PLACE-RARE-PEAKS approximates z(x)-q by epsilon-q||x||^2/(2 sigma^2), then calls its positive region approximately round.
Thus the input profile is parabolic, while the field region has the round geometry used in the next section.
findings.proposed_repair: Near a high peak, the input is nearly parabolic
findings.reason: This keeps the local approximation and high-peak limit while separating height profile from the connected field region.
findings.sidecar_action: Match the section_list title if repaired.
findings.scope: Terminology ambiguity in a retained title; not a new mathematical error in the derivation.

limits: No wholesale prose rewrite is justified. Sufficient connected paragraphs and exact scientific names should remain.
One retained-title terminology ambiguity remains for root decision.
This stage does not approve reader flow, pixels, the whole book or paper reproduction. No edits made.
